summary: The frozen corpus-v2 pin resolves, its mode and bytes remain stable, the no-lock contract is unchanged, the five-entry method roster is in exact append order, and all 21 minimal delta paths are structurally named. V10 does not disambiguate the two different V9-A1 findings, however: its single V9-A1 entry repairs Claude's citation-discipline advisory while Codex's unrelated V9-A1 loses both repair and explicit carry when notFoldedThisSuccessor is removed. That leaves one SHOULD-FIX. Two residual honesty issues are advisory-grade.

shouldFix.title: The closed v10 roster conflates two different V9-A1 findings and silently loses the Codex disposition
shouldFix.detail: The permitted v9 verdicts each contain an advisory named V9-A1, but they are unrelated. Claude V9-A1 is 'citationDiscipline is still written in v6's voice and is three successors stale'. Codex V9-A1 is 'The V8-A3 repair entry imports a v1-verdict-citation defect that belongs to Codex V8-S1'. V10 /appliesFindingsOf accurately enumerates both ids, yet /basedOn/method and repairLog[60] use one unqualified V9-A1. Its verdictTitle and sole operation clearly repair Claude's citationDiscipline finding only. There is no id-collision note, no CODEX-V9-A1 entry, and v10 removes /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor entirely. Codex's advisory remains present in the byte-identical historical repairLog[56], but v10 gives it no repair or carry disposition. The roster is therefore sequence-exact but not finding-unique: one token resolves to two source findings and only one is acted on.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The unresolved source finding was advisory-grade and affects repair attribution rather than the normative schemas, so this is not a blocker. The defect is nevertheless current acceptance-bar audit ambiguity: the artifact explicitly promises a closed repair roster, and this lineage already uses reviewer-qualified ids when collisions occur. A reviewer cannot determine from V9-A1 alone which of the two pinned findings v10 claims to fold.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: In a successor, qualify repairLog[60] and the method roster as CLAUDE-V9-A1. Give Codex V9-A1 an explicit, reviewer-qualified disposition: either repair its attribution concern in a new CODEX-V9-A1 entry or carry it explicitly in appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor. Preserve separate accounting for any older carried advisories rather than deleting their only carry record.

advisories.title: Removing notFoldedThisSuccessor also drops the explicit carry of older unresolved advisories
advisories.detail: V9 explicitly carried Claude V6-A2/A3 through OD-2 and Claude V8-A1/A2 through a no-further-mutation/no-new-accounting-claim undertaking. V10 removes that carry field under the broad META-v10 /appliesFindingsOf amendment. OD-2 itself remains OPEN in namedOpenDecisions, and the /sources and historical repairLog prefixes preserve the V8-A1/A2 conditions, so no normative behavior changes. A successor should restore an explicit carry list or give each older advisory a named disposition.
advisories.notBlocking: All affected findings were advisory-grade, OD-2 remains directly findable, and v10 does not repeat the historical mutations or false accounting relation.

advisories.title: Mode 0444 is a process freeze marker, not technical immutability
advisories.detail: /whatThisDoesNotDo/1 says the 0444 freeze means the digest 'cannot strand by a later silent retarget'. Read-only mode blocks ordinary writes but an owner or writable parent directory can still permit chmod or atomic replacement. The dispatch-level freeze and start/end digest measurements are the actual custody controls. A successor should say 'must not be retargeted while frozen' rather than claim impossibility from file mode.
advisories.notBlocking: The frozen file matched 70248781118452308399e91fcbecb7cac37dd5d58fd03c49ac9efcec445341d5 at review start and throughout the review, retained mode 0444, and was not edited.
